question: Should stale Discord-backed session rows be removed automatically, exposed through an operator/agent cleanup action, or folded into the broader Dashboard prune workflow?
rationale: All viable fixes mutate persistent session state and need product choices about Discord 403 versus 404, transcript retention, permissioning, startup/network cost, and whether agents should be allowed to delete sessions.

options.title: Plugin-owned preview/apply cleanup
options.body: Add a Discord-owned reachability check that previews stale candidates, revalidates before deletion, and uses `sessions.delete` lifecycle semantics for the actual cleanup.

options.title: Operator/Dashboard prune first
options.body: Keep agents read-only and implement the broader explicit prune UI/API first so humans approve destructive cleanup.

options.title: Fold into broader prune issue
options.body: Treat this issue as the Discord/agent-focused facet of the existing Dashboard prune work and resolve both under one maintainer-owned design.

recommendation.title: Plugin-owned preview/apply cleanup
recommendation.body: Add a Discord-owned reachability check that previews stale candidates, revalidates before deletion, and uses `sessions.delete` lifecycle semantics for the actual cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has the most recent merged history across session thread management and Discord thread-binding persistence, making them the strongest routing candidate for the product boundary choice.
